Each phase of the newly proposed guidelines for opening up America have a loosely defined "Gating Criteria” that each State or Region must "Satisfy Before Proceeding to Phased Opening".

Gating criteria has been utilized in the medical industry so it seems innocuous enough, but nonetheless the seeming proximity of Gating with Gates (eg, Bill Gates) had my spidey senses tingling, so I read the document carefully.

The broad definition given to "Gating Criteria" in this document is underwritten by a combination of rubrics to determine "trajectories" of symptoms and cases, as well as hospitals being able to "Treat all patients without crisis care" (p. 2).

(Source: https://www.scribd.com/document/456756096/White-House-guidelines-for-reopening-economy?)

In this article, I am specifically focusing on “crisis care,” which is situated under the third category: hospitals.

The phrase "crisis care" is vague enough that most might graft their own innocuous implications on the seemingly benign medical-like phrase. However, specific vernacular utilized in government documents can drastically affect us on the ground, which is why this phrase piqued my curiosity.

The phrase is only used only once throughout the whole document (p. 2) and never defined. It seems strange that such a particular combination of words—crisis care—is not defined because it occupies an integral fulcrum point within the proposed pathway to re-open America. In the document, the singular usage of "crisis care" exists as an anchor on the "Gating Criteria" threshold for the third category, which pertains to hospitals.

The legal definition (from law insider.com) of "crisis care":

"Crisis Care means an integrated care pathway with uninterrupted round-the-clock emergency access to mental health assessment, home treatment and/or acute inpatient care and psychiatric intensive care unit as required;"

The second definition / same source: https://www.lawinsider.com/dictionary/crisis-care

"Crisis Care means a level of the emergency care credential accessible for court-ordered placement afterhours (4:30 pm to 8am) or during the weekends or holidays by law enforcement, DCYF"

I must admit that I am not a lawyer, but both definitions seem rather ominous. So I did a little more digging.

The Recipe “Xīnjiāng shou zhuā fàn (新疆手抓饭) Asian Lamb Rice”

Ingredients

The Lamb

Chop in big chunks about 2 kg Lamb belly

Spices

1 tsp Cayenne pepper

2 tsp Paprika

About 1/2 tsp Black pepper

About 8 buds of Cardamom "Only the seeds"

Few cloves

1 Tsp Turmeric

1 tsp Coriander seeds

1/2 tsp Cumin seed or powder

1 1/2 tsp Tajine mix (optional)

2 tsp Curry

2 or 3 Bay leaves

Few dry Lime leaves (optional)

Olive oil, about 2 Tsp

Directions

Step 1 - Put the olive oil into a big casserole or a big wok, add the spices and let it start to smoke

Step 2 - Add the lamb and let it cook the lamb for about 35mn to 45 mn in low heat! (Add some water)

Step 3 - Cut in sticks 1.5 kg of carrots and 3 big onions in big chunks

Step 4 - Add the carrots and onions with the Lamb and let it cook for more 30 mn

Step 5 - Add about 3 cups of rice and let it cook for more 20 min

Step 6 - Add about 50gm of raisin and let it cook for more 3 to 5 min

Step 7 - Serve and enjoy
